mechanism: Methylphenidate inhibits reuptake of norepinephrine and dopamine, while amitriptyline blocks reuptake of norepinephrine and serotonin, leading to increased sympathomimetic effects and potential cardiovascular stress; amitriptyline may also inhibit metabolism of methylphenidate via CYP450 enzymes.
action: Monitor blood pressure, heart rate, and cardiac symptoms closely; consider ECG monitoring; adjust doses cautiously and use only when benefits outweigh risks; educate patient on signs of excessive sympathomimetic activation.
